open_points.subject: sandbox own_proc access
open_points.kind: undefined component and conflicting access rule
open_points.text: The formal environment adds `own_proc`, but it is never defined; rule 4 still says the audit hook raises on opening any path outside the exchange directory and read-only runtime.
open_points.question: Does `own_proc` mean a private `/proc` filesystem, and if so may function code read it, or must such reads still produce `sandbox_violation`?
options: Mount a private `/proc` and allow function code to read it.
Mount a private `/proc` for runtime mechanics but trap function code that accesses it.
`own_proc` does not mean a filesystem and grants no additional path access.
open_points.default_guess: Treat `own_proc` as sandbox infrastructure only and keep the stated audit rule: function attempts to open `/proc` are `sandbox_violation`.

witness.initial: An admitted function has a string output and code that reads `/proc/self/stat` and returns part of it.
events: An agent tries the implementation on a valid trial case.
outcomes: The private `own_proc` is readable, so the execution succeeds and returns process information.
The path is outside the exchange directory and runtime, so the audit hook records a trap and the execution concludes `sandbox_violation`.

open_points.subject: repeatable execution order across runs
open_points.text: `When its functions' outputs depend only on their inputs (K-02), the same flow on the same inputs always executes in the same order` conditions the promise only on functions, although operation outputs and outcomes can vary between runs and guards use those outputs.
open_points.question: Is this only a promise that the scheduler chooses deterministically from the nodes that become ready, or is cross-run equality of the executed sequence also promised; if the latter, what additional condition covers changing service outputs and outcomes?
options: The promise concerns only deterministic scheduling within a run; different service results may produce different executed sequences.
The full sequence repeats only when function outputs and all operation outputs and outcomes repeat.
The full sequence must repeat from flow inputs alone, despite changing service responses.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the rule as deterministic scheduling of the ready work, not as a guarantee that separate runs execute the same sequence when service results differ.

witness.initial: A proven active flow has no function nodes. A read operation `R` returns data plus a closed guard value; one value enables operation node `a`, and another enables operation node `b`. Both runs use the same flow inputs.
events: An agent starts run 1; the service returns the guard value enabling `a`.
The agent starts run 2 with the same inputs; the service returns the guard value enabling `b`.
outcomes: Under the guard and service rules, run 1 executes `R,a` while run 2 executes `R,b`.
Under the changed consequence, the condition on function outputs is vacuously satisfied, so both runs are promised to execute in the same order.
witness.observer: The owner or agent reading the two traces.
